title: Coface and fixed retraction identities for the polynomial additive bar
statement:
For a commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebra $B$ and an integer $r\geq0$, define the nonnegative cochain complex $P_{B,r}$ by
$$P_{B,r}^n=B[x_{a,i}:1\leq a\leq n,\ 1\leq i\leq r],\qquad n\geq0,$$
using polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Write $x_a=(x_{a,1},\ldots,x_{a,r})$. Its differential is
$$(df)(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+1})=f(x_2,\ldots,x_{n+1})+\sum_{a=1}^{n}(-1)^a f(x_1,\ldots,x_a+x_{a+1},\ldots,x_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(x_1,\ldots,x_n).$$
In degree zero the first and last terms cancel. Put $P^n=0$ for $n<0$.

Let $K_{B,r}^q$ be the free $B$-module on $e_I$ for subsets $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of cardinality $q$, with zero differential and zero terms for $q<0$ or $q>r$. Define $i:K_{B,r}\to P_{B,r}$ by $i(e_\varnothing)=1$ and
$$i(e_{\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}})=x_{1,i_1}\cdots x_{q,i_q}.$$
Define $p^0=1_B$. For $q>0$, define $p^q$ on a polynomial monomial to be zero unless every block $x_a$ has total degree one and these degree-one coordinates have pairwise distinct indices $j_1,\ldots,j_q$. In that remaining case set
$$p^q(x_{1,j_1}\cdots x_{q,j_q})=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)e_{\{j_1,\ldots,j_q\}},$$
where $(j_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,j_{\sigma(q)})$ is increasingly ordered. Extend $B$-linearly. Then the cofaces defining $d$ satisfy $\delta^b\delta^a=\delta^a\delta^{b-1}$ for $a<b$, and
$$d^0=0,\qquad d^{n+1}d^n=0,\qquad d^qi^q=0,\qquad p^{q+1}d^q=0,\qquad p^qi^q=1_{K^q}.$$
Every map preserves total coordinate multidegree: give $x_{a,j}$ multidegree the $j$-th unit vector and $e_I$ multidegree $1_I$. These formulas hold over every commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebra, including the zero algebra. For $r=0$, $P^n=B$ in every nonnegative degree and $d^n=0$ for even $n$, $d^n=1_B$ for odd $n$.

proof.text: Write $\delta_n^a:P^n\to P^{n+1}$ for the substitutions in the displayed differential, with $0\leq a\leq n+1$. By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] each is a $B$-algebra map, hence $B$-linear. In degree zero both substitutions are the structure map $B\to P^1$, so $d^0=\delta_0^0-\delta_0^1=0$. The specified values of $i$ and $p$ extend uniquely $B$-linearly on the indicated free bases; in particular $i^0=p^0=1_B$ under $P^0=K^0=B$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image algebraic obligation; agent calculation, step 1 (the blueprint does not assert this polynomial identity).

proof.text: Check the coface identity by substitution, not by evaluating polynomial functions on $B$-points. In $P^{n+2}$ put $v_0=0$ and $v_t=x_1+\cdots+x_t$. The consecutive differences of $(v_0,\ldots,v_{n+2})$ are the formal blocks $x_t$. Deleting vertex $v_a$ replaces these differences by precisely the face tuple: omit the first block if $a=0$, merge $x_a+x_{a+1}$ if $0<a<n+2$, and omit the last if $a=n+2$. Translating the remaining vertices by their first vertex changes no differences. For $a<b$, deleting $v_b$ then $v_a$ leaves exactly the same ordered vertices as deleting $v_a$ then vertex $b-1$ of the remaining list. Thus both composites substitute identical sums of formal blocks for every generator, and fix coefficients. The uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives $\delta_{n+1}^b\delta_n^a=\delta_{n+1}^a\delta_n^{b-1}$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image algebraic obligation; agent calculation, step 2 (the blueprint does not assert this polynomial identity).

proof.text: Expand the two differentials into the alternating sums of cofaces. On the finite index set Fin(n+2) × Fin(n+3), split into the pairs (i,j) with j≤i and their complement. The bijection (i,j) ↦ (j,i+1) identifies the two parts. The coface identity identifies the composites, while the exponents of -1 differ by one. Cancel the paired terms. This is the finite-sum argument of Mathlib AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComplex.d_squared, applied directly to the polynomial substitutions without building a cosimplicial object.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image algebraic obligation; agent calculation, step 3 (the blueprint does not assert this polynomial identity).

proof.text: For any tuple j:Fin(q)→Fin(r), let M_k be the product with the k-th block omitted. The first coface of the coordinate product is M_0 and the last is M_q. In an inner coface only its indexed factor splits: isolate that factor with Finset.mul_prod_erase and distribute to get M_a+M_(a+1). Mathlib Fin.sum_neg_one_pow_eq_zero telescopes their signed sum to zero, including q=0. Apply Finsupp.lhom_ext to extend from subset basis vectors to the inclusion map.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image algebraic obligation; agent calculation, step 4 (the blueprint does not assert this polynomial identity).

proof.text: Expand the explicitly constructed projection as the sum, over injective tuples j, of coeff(coordinateExponent j,f) times its signed subset vector; this follows from Basis.constr_apply by exchanging the finite sums. A substitution omitting an output block has zero coefficient at every coordinateExponent j: a renamed exponent has value zero at that block, whereas coordinateExponent j has value one there. Thus both outer substitutions have zero projection. For each inner merge, swapping the two output blocks fixes its polynomial by commutativity of addition.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image algebraic obligation; agent calculation, step 5 (the blueprint does not assert this polynomial identity).

proof.text: For injective j define F_j(a,b) to be 1 if j(a)<j(b), -1 if j(b)<j(a), and 0 on equality. This is antisymmetric. Rewrite sortingSign(j) as the product of F_j(a,b) over a<b. Mathlib Equiv.Perm.prod_Ioi_comp_eq_sign_mul_prod shows that precomposing j by a permutation multiplies this product by the permutation sign. In particular a transposition negates it. Pair tuples j and j composed with the transposition of the two merged blocks, using Finset.sum_involution. The coefficient is unchanged because the polynomial is fixed by the corresponding block renaming; their coordinate subsets agree and their signs are opposite. Noninjective tuples have zero summand, and an injective tuple cannot be fixed by a nontrivial transposition. Hence each merge has zero projection. By linearity, the full differential has zero projection. No division or nonzero-ring hypothesis is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image algebraic obligation; agent calculation, step 6 (the blueprint does not assert this polynomial identity).

proof.text: The coordinate exponent determines its tuple by evaluating it at each block-coordinate pair. Therefore on a coordinate product the projection has exactly one contributing tuple. For the increasing tuple supplied by Finset.orderEmbOfFin, its coordinateSubset is the original subset and every inversion factor is 1. Thus projection sends each included subset basis vector back to itself. Finsupp.lhom_ext proves projection composed with inclusion is the identity, including the empty subset and the case q>r.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image algebraic obligation; agent calculation, step 7 (the blueprint does not assert this polynomial identity).

proof.text: Use weighted-homogeneous induction on polynomials. Evaluation of a monomial is a scalar times a product of powers of the images of its variables. Every coface image of a variable has the same coordinate unit weight, so cofaces preserve weight, and closure of each weighted-homogeneous submodule under sums and scalar multiplication proves the same for d. The weight of coordinateExponent(j) is the indicator of coordinateSubset(j) when j is injective. This proves weight preservation of inclusion by expanding its finite basis sum and of projection by homogeneous monomial induction. For negative integer degrees use HomologicalComplex.isZero_extend_X and the nonnegativity of natural numbers. For q>r, cardinality bounds make ExteriorIndex empty and hence its Finsupp module subsingleton. At r=0, use MvPolynomial.eq_C_of_isEmpty and Fin.sum_neg_one_pow: every coface fixes constants and the alternating scalar sum has the stated parity.

lean.statement: theorem coface_retraction_identities (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra ℚ B] (r : ℕ) : (∀ (n : ℕ) (a b : Fin (n + 2)), a ≤ b → (coface B r (n + 1) b.succ).comp (coface B r n a) = (coface B r (n + 1) a.castSucc).comp (coface B r n b)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, differential B r n = ∑ a : Fin (n + 2), (-1 : B) ^ a.val • (coface B r n a).toLinearMap) ∧ differential B r 0 = 0 ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, (differential B r (n + 1)).comp (differential B r n) = 0) ∧ (∀ q : ℕ, (differential B r q).comp (inclusion B r q) = 0) ∧ (∀ q : ℕ, (projection B r (q + 1)).comp (differential B r q) = 0) ∧ (∀ q : ℕ, (projection B r q).comp (inclusion B r q) = LinearMap.id) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin (n + 2)) (m : Fin r → ℕ) (f : P B r n), MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous (coordinateWeight r n) f m → MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous (coordinateWeight r (n + 1)) (coface B r n a f) m) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (m : Fin r → ℕ) (f : P B r n), MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous (coordinateWeight r n) f m → MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous (coordinateWeight r (n + 1)) (differential B r n f) m) ∧ (∀ (q : ℕ) (m : Fin r → ℕ) (v : K B r q), ExteriorHomogeneous B r q v m → MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous (coordinateWeight r q) (inclusion B r q v) m) ∧ (∀ (q : ℕ) (m : Fin r → ℕ) (f : P B r q), MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous (coordinateWeight r q) f m → ExteriorHomogeneous B r q (projection B r q f) m) ∧ (∀ z : ℤ, z < 0 → CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero ((polynomialComplex B r).X z) ∧ CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero ((exteriorComplex B r).X z)) ∧ (∀ q : ℕ, r < q → Subsingleton (K B r q)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (f : P B 0 n), differential B 0 n f = if Even n then 0 else MvPolynomial.C (MvPolynomial.coeff 0 f))
